problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A,\,D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of $z={x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 1.$ What is the missing expression?
worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z={x}^{2}+2{y}^{2},\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1.
$$

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+2{y}^{2})=2x, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+2{y}^{2})=4y,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(2x)^{2}+(4y)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+4{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is $\sqrt{1+4{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2}}.$
